name: Your World of AMEX
overview:
Your World of AMEX (YWOA) was a project developed with DCG One for American Express, highlighting the benefits of Green, Gold, and Platinum cards. The Augmented Reality experience featured a 3D island rising from under the ground, divided into four quadrants showcasing Travel, Personal, Hotel and Dining benefits. A voice-over assistant guided users through the benefits, while SLAM elements, tappable easter eggs and animated 2D/3D assets added interactivity and engagement.

We optimized the experience for a wide range of devices, ranging from the iPhone 8 released in 2017 to modern Apple and Android phones and tablets, balancing texture quality to ensure smooth performance and preventing crashes on low-end devices whithout compromising visuals and quality on high-end devices. Accessibility options were also implemented for users who required them.

As the primary contributor in this project, I integrated 2D and 3D assets provided by the respective creative teams at both Aircards and DCG One. I developed interactive elements, CTAs, UI components and made multiple quality checks to ensure smooth performance across the aforementioned range of devices. I also oversaw database design and population, ensuring seamless integration for both our team at Aircards and the developer at DCG One. I also participated in weekly meetings with DCG One to report progress, review feature updates and fixes, and brainstorm solutions to feedback from the American Express creative team.
impact: * The AR experience greatly impressed American Express executives in its high-quality design and innovative advertisement approach, prompting them to greenlight a second project mid-development, demonstrating the value and effectiveness of the immersive experience.

name: Easter Happiness Hunt
overview:
The Haribo Easter Happiness Hunt was a WebAR event that spanned three annual Easter timeframes promoting Haribo's Easter candy product line. The event featured an augmented reality scavenger hunt where six different candies would be hidden behind various obstacles. The obstacles appeared in the player's environment through their device camera using SLAM technology and by moving through the environment with their device, the player could find candy hidden behind bushes, trees and fences. By reaching the game's end via different annual goals, the player would be prompted to enter their for a contest to win Haribo's Easter products.

This project evolved over the three annual events, each introducing fresh improvements to the core gameplay loop to enhance player engagement. In the first year, players were tasked with finding six candies hidden throughout the environment. Collecting all six within the time limit resulted in victory. While it was simple, it was intended to be easy for children to complete. The second year expanded on this concept by shifting the goal to collecting as many candies as possible within the time limit. This introduced a completitive element, allowing players to compare their scores and to compete to achieve the highest total score. In the third year, the experience advanced even further with the addition of a multiplayer mode. Players were connected through a host-peer network, with the host acting as the source of truth for synchronizing candy collection across devices. This was done to prevent different players from collecting the same piece of candy and potential discrepancies between the host and peer's scores. At the end of each session, the player with the highest candy count was crowned the winner.

As the primary contributor for this project, I integrated all 2D and 3D assets provided by the respective creative teams but made edits to UI elements and 3D assets as necessary to keep performance uniform across various devices. I implemented the majority of the core game logic, enabling the project to run smoothly. While the multiplayer system was adapted from a colleague's previous implementation in a different project, I reconfigured and integrated it to meet this project's specific requirements.

* 25.6% form submission rate (1st party data collection via Google Analytics)
* 14.8% experience share rate
* 7.6 click-through rate to brand website

name: #AnnounceYourself
overview:
#AnnounceYourself was a WebAR project developed in conjunction with AND THE NEW and Manchester City to promote the partnership between Manchester City and Tecno Mobile. Utilizing a 360 environment, the user could visit various places, such as the Etihad Stadium, the Man City training grounds and the press conference room. The main experience featured a tour of the Manchester City facillities, allowing the user to immerse themselves in how a player would be signed to the team. From meeting their future teammates to being able to customize their own name and number to be put on an avatar and ultimately playing in a penalty shootout minigame, the user could personalize their experience from start to finish, ultimately meeting Pep Guardiola and hold a press conference to sign with the team. 

As this was my first project for Aircards, I had help from my colleagues to develop the project, but ultimately the development was led by myself to integrate all the assets and develop the overall experience to completion. For this project, I was in charge of integrating the creative assets to the UI, developing the main tour and environmental areas, and designing the penalty shootout minigame.

name: Where Performance Meets Purpose
overview:
Owens Corning: Where Performance Meets Purpose was a WebAR experience designed to showcase the range of Owens Corning products used throughout a building. Each product was integrated into a 3D building model that could be revealed by tapping its corresponding hotspot, causing it to emerge from the structure like a puzzle piece. Once selected, the product played an animation loop demonstrating its installation process, accompanied by an on-screen description. The experience also used SLAM-based tracking to anchor the building to the user's physical environment, allowing users to walk around the structure and explore it from different angles.

As the primary contributor for this project, I was responsible for integrating the 3D assets and copy updates throughout the building and product experiences. The initial concept featured camera animations that would guide users from an overview of the building toward a specific product, zooming in as the product emerged from the building. However, this approach presented technical challenges, as the animation could fail to land on the correct position depending on the user's camera angle and position. To provide a more reliable experience, we ultimately separated the product showcase into its own scene. Users could focus on the product independently and return to the building environment whenever they wanted.
technicalDetails: WebAR experience developed with Three.js, A-Frame, 8th Wall and JavaScript
responsibilities:
Primary Contributor: 
* Integrated the key logic for the hotspots and UI elements and developed several iterations of the (scrapped) camera angle movement logic. 
* Designed and deployed several changes and fixes to the SLAM-based tracking in order to minimize the tracking drift and jitter, ensuring that it was as infrequent and imperceptible as possible. 
* Implemented additional features into a colleague’s external hotspot scene implementation, optimizing the scene transition for a faster and smoother user experience.

Quality Assurance:
* Ensured stable performance and high visual fidelity through multiple texture optimization passes, balancing file size and visual quality. 
* Developed camera-relative positional and rotational checks to support the hotspot to camera movement logic, improving accuracy and consistency to the intended position and rotation values.
* Conducted extensive testing across a wide range of physical Apple and Android devices, as well as emulators, to ensure UI elements scaled and remained properly positioned across a range of device sizes and screen resolutions.

name: Spin Genie Treasure Quest
overview:
Spin Genie Treasure Quest was a 3D WebAR scavenger hunt experience. The project began with an interactive genie lamp; rubbing the lamp triggered an animation that transported users inside. After reading the game instructions, a 60-second timer began, accompanied by a matching falling-sand animation. Users could move their device or swipe the screen to explore the environment and locate five hidden objects, each themed around a different Spin Genie slot machine. To prevent frustration, if there was a five second duration between the last object found, a hint arrow pointing to the direction of the object would be shown. Once all five objects were found, or when the timer expired, the experience presented a registration form where users could claim bonus spins, with successful completion rewarding additional spins.

As the primary contributor, I was responsible for building the core experience from start to finish, including the game mechanics, interactive elements, and the registration form used to claim bonus spins.  I also implemented the project's analytics and identified a significant drop-off during the initial experience. Based on these insights, we removed the opening animation and streamlined the user journey by taking users directly into the game, reducing friction and improving access to the core experience.
technicalDetails: WebAR experience developed with Three.js, A-Frame, 8th Wall and JavaScript
responsibilities:
Primary Contributor: 
* Built the core experience logic and implemented animation and interactive elements. 
* Refined the gameplay experience by finding a balance between skill and fun while implementing hint features to assist users in locating objects when they struggled to progress. 
* Ideated and implemented an accessibility feature for users who may be unable to physically rotate their device, providing an alternate swipe-based interaction to control the camera rotation.

Quality Assurance:
* Ensured stable performance and high visual fidelity by optimizing the texture files to balance between file size and visual quality. 
* Integrated Google Analytics into the project and collaborated closely with the analytical team to highlight user pain points and drop-off rates. 
* Utilized the insights gleamed from the analytical data to iterate quickly on the experience, removing and refining elements that contributed to the drop-off.

name: Dare Rainforest Alliance
overview:
The Dare Iced Coffee AR experience was a WebAR activation developed in collaboration with Yahoo Creative Studios and Dare Iced Coffee, bringing their Rainforest Alliance Certified bottles to life through SLAM-based tracking. Users could scan a tabletop or similar surface and tap the screen to place the bottle and surrounding rainforest environment into their physical space. An animated red-eyed tree frog would then hop around the bottle, while tapping a pile of coffee beans triggered an interactive animation revealing the Rainforest Alliance Certified logo. Users could also tap a CTA at any point to capture a screenshot of the experience with a branded watermark and share it on social media.

name: Full Fibre House
overview:
The EE Full Fibre House was a WebAR experience developed for EE, a UK telecommunications company, to showcase the benefits of its Full Fibre service and demonstrate how it provides fast, reliable connectivity throughout the home. The experience consisted of two interconnected components: a physical Full Fibre House, a wooden house-shaped installation featuring 2D images representing each room, and the accompanying WebAR experience. Users could scan the images within each room to trigger an animation showcasing how Full Fibre enhanced connectivity in that area of the home. During each animation, 2D information panels would appear to provide additional details about the featured feature.

As the primary contributor for the project, I was responsible for building the core experience from start to finish, integrating the creative assets, developing the scripts that enabled smooth animations to trigger following each scan, and ensuring that each room's image could be reliably detected across different devices. I also worked with internal teams to evaluate performance across a range of devices and monitor user engagement throughout the experience.

name: Shirt of Firsts
overview:
The Shirt of Firsts was a desktop 3D experience developed in conjunction with GOAL and Unilever to promote 22 "first" achievements during the 2022 FIFA World Cup. The experience initially featured a blank shirt, with 22 different patches updating on the shirt during various moments in the World Cup. Each patch featured a different country with a historic "first" milestone. The user was able to click on each individual patch to read what the milestone was. An additional contest was held to give out a physical Shirt of Firsts to a lucky winner.

As the primary contributor of this project, I designed the system to easily swap out assets for the Shirt of Firsts, which contained 22 different texture files and infomation points that would be updated during various times in December when this project was active. I partnered with the back-end developer to co-design the CMS system, allowing the client to easily upload information for each milestone to be updated internally on the website.

name: Secret Santa Postal Service
overview:
Cadbury: Secret Santa Postal Service was a mobile WebAR experience developed in partnership with Bernadette to promote the annual Secret Santa Postal Service campaign to give away free chocolate bars to recipients across the UK. This iteration featured an Augmented Reality activation where the poster would expand out to show a counter nook with the postal worker introducing the campaign. After the introduction, the user would be able to enter the promotion to give away a Cadbury chocolate bar away to the recipient of their choice. 

As the primary contributor, I designed the Augmented Reality activation by integrating creative assets and developed interactive scripts to allow the experience to run smoothly. I also aided in brainstorming accessibility features so users who were hard of hearing could also participate in the experience. Through this, I developed a script to sync the video with subtitles, which would activate if the user chose to activate it.
